operative_clauses.judgment_reason: The sole paragraph of Executive Order 8341 says that Executive Order No. 8323 of January 22, 1940 "is hereby revoked." It is a present-tense, self-executing revocation with no deferred effective date, condition or continuing duty, so the command was performed and ended when the order was signed on February 8, 1940, the date printed in the held text. The filing date (February 9, 1940) and the issue date (February 10, 1940) are alternative readings, and none moves the end outside February 1940. The revocation of Executive Order No. 8323 remains as a surviving effect of the completed act. No held instrument revokes, amends or extends Executive Order 8341.

Executive Order 8341 of February 8, 1940 (5 FR 643, Federal Register issue of Saturday, February 10, 1940; FR Doc. 40-606, filed February 9, 1940) is a single paragraph. Its only operative act is to revoke Executive Order No. 8323 of January 22, 1940, which had abolished Customs Collection District No. 43 (Tennessee), revoked the designations of Memphis, Chattanooga and Nashville as customs ports of entry, and extended the limits of Customs Collection District No. 42 (Kentucky) and Customs Collection District No. 45 (St. Louis). Identity rests on the heading, the signing date, the Federal Register document line and the page; the machine-extracted text prints the closing order-number line with a stray character and omits the number from the heading, which the packet records as a segmentation lead. The loss of port-of-entry status is a surviving effect of that executed act.
